meta.move: Strong path to agreement with a deadline said aloud
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty-five minutes. My son found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, Hale, and on what basis?
I owe you an apology: I put the zero in before calling you. That was my mistake.
Okay. Was Owen heard before you entered it? And what do you have besides a machine's opinion?
On November 2 I asked Owen what 'epistemological paralysis' means. He said 'like, being stuck', and he couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that down the same day.

You wrote that down the same day. Then show me the note, with the date on it, and tell me whether Owen knew that conversation would decide his mark. A seventeen-year-old asked a vocabulary question cold, out of nowhere, proves he was put on the spot, Hale.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.

I'm writing down October 15. Do you have the outline here, with his name and the date on it, so I can read it myself? Students change their minds between an outline and a final draft, Hale; that's what drafting is.
Here's my offer: a supervised rewrite, Thursday at 8:15 in my room. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll send you that in writing by Friday at 3 PM.

You still haven't shown me the outline. Whatever happens, this stays off his record and it stays quiet, so tell me whether anything is on file right now and who besides you decides whether it "holds up." And I want those terms in writing before Thursday at 8:15, not after.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In our meeting you offered Owen a supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15 in your room, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record, and you said you would confirm this in writing by Friday at 3 PM. I still require the October 15 outline for my own review, confirmation that nothing is on his record now, and an assurance that this stays private and off his record whatever happens. I expect those terms in writing before Thursday at 8:15.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: fallback position, insisting it stays off his record and stays quiet, with the rewrite offered but not yet accepted.
What moved her: the October 15 outline arguing cowardice, which the essay never mentions.
